title: Extend one infinitesimal quotient inverse by square-zero lifting
statement:
Let $\varphi:A\to C$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, let $J\subseteq C$ be an ideal, and suppose $A\to C/J$ is surjective with kernel $I$. Assume that for every commutative $A$-algebra $E$ and ideal $N\subseteq E$ with $N^2=0$, reduction induces a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{A\text{-alg}}(C,E)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{A\text{-alg}}(C,E/N)$. Quotients, ideal powers and algebra maps have the meanings of [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. For $m\ge1$, put $f_m:A/I^m\to C/J^m$, $[a]\mapsto[\varphi(a)]$, and let $\pi_{I,m}$ and $\pi_{J,m}$ be the quotient maps from $A$ and $C$. Fix an integer $n\ge1$ and assume $f_n$ is an isomorphism with inverse $g_n$. Write $r_n:A/I^{n+1}\to A/I^n$ and $s_n:C/J^{n+1}\to C/J^n$ for reduction. There is a unique $A$-algebra map $\ell:C\to A/I^{n+1}$ with $r_n\ell=g_n\pi_{J,n}$. It satisfies $\ell(J)\subseteq I/I^{n+1}$ and $\ell(J^{n+1})=0$. Its induced map $g_{n+1}:C/J^{n+1}\to A/I^{n+1}$ satisfies
$$g_{n+1}f_{n+1}=\mathrm{id},\qquad f_{n+1}g_{n+1}=\mathrm{id},\qquad r_ng_{n+1}=g_ns_n.$$
No finiteness, Noetherianity or equality $J=IC$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0H1D (lemma-formally-etale-lift-infinitesimal), proof: one successive dotted arrow, its factorization and the uniqueness argument for the inverse composite.

proof.text: Since $I=\varphi^{-1}(J)$, products and sums give $\varphi(I^m)\subseteq J^m$. Thus $f_m([a])=[\varphi(a)]$ is well defined. These maps commute with reductions by evaluation on representatives. Also $g_n$ is an $A$-algebra map: $g_n(\pi_{J,n}\varphi(a))=g_nf_n(\pi_{I,n}(a))=\pi_{I,n}(a)$.

source.place: Tag 0H1D (lemma-formally-etale-lift-infinitesimal), proof: one successive dotted arrow, its factorization and the uniqueness argument for the inverse composite.

proof.text: Put $E=A/I^{n+1}$ and $N=I^n/I^{n+1}$. Reduction $r_n$ has kernel $N$, and $E/N\cong A/I^n$: the maps $[[a]_{I^{n+1}}]_N\mapsto[a]_{I^n}$ and $[a]_{I^n}\mapsto[[a]_{I^{n+1}}]_N$ are well defined inverse algebra maps. Products of two representatives from $I^n$ belong to $I^{2n}\subseteq I^{n+1}$, since $n\ge1$, so $N^2=0$.

source.place: Tag 0H1D (lemma-formally-etale-lift-infinitesimal), proof: one successive dotted arrow, its factorization and the uniqueness argument for the inverse composite.

proof.text: The assumed bijection, applied to this $E,N$ and the $A$-algebra map $g_n\pi_{J,n}:C\to A/I^n\cong E/N$, gives a unique $A$-algebra map $\ell:C\to A/I^{n+1}$ with $r_n\ell=g_n\pi_{J,n}$. This is a direct application of the stated hypothesis, with no theorem about formal etaleness invoked.

source.place: Tag 0H1D (lemma-formally-etale-lift-infinitesimal), proof: one successive dotted arrow, its factorization and the uniqueness argument for the inverse composite.

proof.text: For $j\in J$, choose $a\in A$ with $\ell(j)=[a]_{I^{n+1}}$. The lifting equality gives $[a]_{I^n}=g_n([j]_{J^n})$, hence $[\varphi(a)]_{J^n}=[j]_{J^n}$. Therefore $\varphi(a)-j\in J^n\subseteq J$ and $a\in I$. Thus $\ell(J)\subseteq I/I^{n+1}$. Every product of $n+1$ elements of $J$ is killed by $\ell$, since its image is a product of $n+1$ classes from $I$. Sums and multiples give $\ell(J^{n+1})=0$.

source.place: Tag 0H1D (lemma-formally-etale-lift-infinitesimal), proof: one successive dotted arrow, its factorization and the uniqueness argument for the inverse composite.

proof.text: Define $g_{n+1}([c]_{J^{n+1}})=\ell(c)$. It is well defined because $\ell$ kills $J^{n+1}$; its algebra laws follow from those of $\ell$. On $[a]_{I^{n+1}}$, its composite with $f_{n+1}$ is $\ell(\varphi(a))=[a]_{I^{n+1}}$ by $A$-linearity of $\ell$. Hence $g_{n+1}f_{n+1}=\mathrm{id}$.

source.place: Tag 0H1D (lemma-formally-etale-lift-infinitesimal), proof: one successive dotted arrow, its factorization and the uniqueness argument for the inverse composite.

proof.text: In $E'=C/J^{n+1}$ put $N'=J^n/J^{n+1}$. As in Step 2, $N'^2=0$ and $E'/N'\cong C/J^n$, with quotient map $s_n$. The two $A$-algebra maps $u=f_{n+1}\ell$ and $v=\pi_{J,n+1}$ from $C$ satisfy $s_nu=f_nr_n\ell=f_ng_n\pi_{J,n}=\pi_{J,n}=s_nv$. Injectivity in the assumed lifting bijection for $E',N'$ gives $u=v$. On every $[c]_{J^{n+1}}$, this says $f_{n+1}g_{n+1}([c])=[c]$, proving the other inverse identity.

source.place: Tag 0H1D (lemma-formally-etale-lift-infinitesimal), proof: one successive dotted arrow, its factorization and the uniqueness argument for the inverse composite.

proof.text: Finally, for every $[c]_{J^{n+1}}$, the defining lift equality gives $r_ng_{n+1}([c])=r_n\ell(c)=g_n\pi_{J,n}(c)=g_ns_n([c])$. Quotient representatives exhaust the domain, so $r_ng_{n+1}=g_ns_n$. All power containments used above follow from $n\ge1$ and ideal multiplication; neither $J=IC$ nor any finiteness hypothesis was used.

lean.statement: theorem formallyEtale_powerStep {A : Type u} {C : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing C] [Algebra A C] (I : Ideal A) (J : Ideal C) (hI : I = J.comap (algebraMap A C)) (hsurj : Function.Surjective ((Ideal.Quotient.mk J).comp (algebraMap A C))) (hlift : ∀ (E : Type (max u v)) [CommRing E] [Algebra A E] (N : Ideal E), N ^ 2 = ⊥ → Function.Bijective (fun h : C →ₐ[A] E ↦ (Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ A N).comp h)) (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) (g : C ⧸ J ^ n →+* A ⧸ I ^ n) (hleft : g.comp (Ideal.quotientMap (J ^ n) (algebraMap A C) ((pow_le_pow_left' hI.le n).trans (Ideal.le_comap_pow (algebraMap A C) n))) = RingHom.id (A ⧸ I ^ n)) (hright : (Ideal.quotientMap (J ^ n) (algebraMap A C) ((pow_le_pow_left' hI.le n).trans (Ideal.le_comap_pow (algebraMap A C) n))).comp g = RingHom.id (C ⧸ J ^ n)) : ∃ ell : C →ₐ[A] A ⧸ I ^ (n + 1), (Ideal.Quotient.factor (Ideal.pow_le_pow_right (Nat.le_succ n))).comp ell.toRingHom = g.comp (Ideal.Quotient.mk (J ^ n)) ∧ (∀ ell' : C →ₐ[A] A ⧸ I ^ (n + 1), (Ideal.Quotient.factor (Ideal.pow_le_pow_right (Nat.le_succ n))).comp ell'.toRingHom = g.comp (Ideal.Quotient.mk (J ^ n)) → ell' = ell) ∧ (∀ j : C, j ∈ J → ∃ a : A, a ∈ I ∧ Ideal.Quotient.mk (I ^ (n + 1)) a = ell j) ∧ (∀ c : C, c ∈ J ^ (n + 1) → ell c = 0) ∧ ∃ gnext : C ⧸ J ^ (n + 1) →+* A ⧸ I ^ (n + 1), gnext.comp (Ideal.Quotient.mk (J ^ (n + 1))) = ell.toRingHom ∧ gnext.comp (Ideal.quotientMap (J ^ (n + 1)) (algebraMap A C) ((pow_le_pow_left' hI.le (n + 1)).trans (Ideal.le_comap_pow (algebraMap A C) (n + 1)))) = RingHom.id (A ⧸ I ^ (n + 1)) ∧ (Ideal.quotientMap (J ^ (n + 1)) (algebraMap A C) ((pow_le_pow_left' hI.le (n + 1)).trans (Ideal.le_comap_pow (algebraMap A C) (n + 1)))).comp gnext = RingHom.id (C ⧸ J ^ (n + 1)) ∧ (Ideal.Quotient.factor (Ideal.pow_le_pow_right (Nat.le_succ n))).comp gnext = g.comp (Ideal.Quotient.factor (Ideal.pow_le_pow_right (Nat.le_succ n)))
